artworks.title: The Monkey Room in the Tower
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of monkeys interacting in a room. The scene is titled "The Monkey Room in the Tower." Several monkeys are engaging in various activities around a blazing fire in a fireplace. Some monkeys are perched on shelves and ledges, observing the scene, while others are near the fire, seemingly interacting with logs. The room is depicted with ornamental grids on the walls, suggesting a cage-like setting. The composition captures the monkeys' interactions in this confined space.

artworks.title: Dr. Botherum, the Mountebank
artworks.description: This is a painting of a crowded scene with characters interacting in various ways in what looks like a fair or market setting. There is a central platform where characters are engaging in activities, including a tooth extraction, with others watching or participating. The crowd below is diverse, with some eating, conversing, and bartering. The overall mood is lively and humorous, reminiscent of social scenes from the past, in a style similar to that of Thomas Rowlandson.

artworks.title: Hocus Pocus, or Searching for the Philosopher's Stone
artworks.medium: etching, aquatint, and stipple with hand coloring on wove paper
artworks.description: This is a painting of an alchemist's workshop scene. The image depicts an interior space cluttered with various alchemical apparatuses and items associated with an old-fashioned laboratory. There is a central figure observing a process in progress within a glowing furnace. Another figure is operating a bellows to encourage the fire. Smoke and steam rise around them. Various vessels, including bottles and kettles, are scattered around the room. In the background, figures are engaged in different activities.

artworks.title: Downfall of Monopoly in 1800
artworks.description:
This is a drawing depicting a chaotic scene involving the downfall of monopoly in 1800. The image shows a crowded caricature with dynamic, exaggerated movements. On the left side, a group of men representing different commodities are struggling and being swept away. Each man is dressed in distinctive 18th-century attire with expressions of shock or distress. A skeletal figure on a horse, referencing Death, ominously moves through the crowd, whipping them along. 

On the right side, there is a more serene atmosphere with women and children basking in light. A large statue holding a trident symbolizes justice or authority, overseeing the scene. Sailing ships are visible in the distant sea under a bright sky. 

The artwork is rich in satire, exaggerating the figures to amplify the drama and turmoil associated with the end of monopolistic control during the period.

artworks.title: Odd-Characters
artworks.description: The image features a collection of various characters' heads, each with distinct expressions and hairstyles. The characters are closely packed together, each visible from the shoulders up. They are arranged in a diamond-shaped pattern formed by intersecting lines. The heads display a variety of facial features and hair styles, including sideburns, mustaches, beards, wigs, and hats with feathers. Some characters wear hats like tricorns, berets, and helmets, while others show different facial expressions. Three women can be identified by hairstyles adorned with flowers or ribbons, and one of them is wearing a pearl necklace. The background of the image is plain. The composition is labeled "Odd-Characters."

artworks.title: The Lawyers Last Circuit
artworks.description: This is a drawing of skeletons riding skeletal horses with a panic-stricken man. The image depicts four skeletons on horseback, galloping through a fiery landscape. One of the skeletons is holding a terrified man in black clothing, who is in mid-air as if being tossed from a horse. The drawing includes a signpost pointing "ROAD TO HELL". The sky is reddish-orange, adding to the dramatic atmosphere of the scene. The artwork is titled "THE LAWYERS LAST CIRCUIT," and includes a quote from Shakespeare's "Hamlet".

artworks.title: One Tree Hill, Greenwich Park
artworks.description: This is a painting depicting a lively scene on a hill in a park. The image shows a bustling scene atop a grassy hill, where people are engaged in various activities. The landscape includes trees framing the hill, with details of lush foliage. Figures in dynamic poses are scattered across the hill, suggesting movement such as running, tumbling, or engaging in playful antics. The colors are vivid, with individuals wearing bright attire. The title at the bottom of the artwork indicates the location as 'One Tree Hill, Greenwich Park.' The painting has a lively and slightly humorous characteristic typical of late 18th to early 19th-century caricature and is in the style of Thomas Rowlandson.

artworks.title: Running
artworks.medium: hand-colored etching and aquatint with blue wash
artworks.description: This is a painting of a horse race in a countryside setting. The scene includes numerous horses and riders galloping towards the finish line. A crowd of spectators is depicted in the foreground, with some standing and others sitting or reclining on the grass, watching the race. There are carriages and horses close to the spectators. The background shows the countryside under a blue sky with clouds. The painting is detailed, showing the postures of the onlookers and the motion of the racing horses. This is in the style of Thomas Rowlandson.

artworks.title: Running
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a horse race with a crowd of spectators surrounding the race. The drawing shows several horses and riders racing across an open field, with spectators watching the event. On each side of the race, there are groups of elegantly dressed spectators, some standing and some sitting. The drawing conveys movement and excitement, with the horses galloping and the crowd engaged with the race. The background includes hills, adding depth to the setting. The scene indicates a lively social gathering, possibly at a country fair, depicted with detailed line work.

artworks.title: Dressing for a Birthday
artworks.description: This is a painting of a group of people preparing for a social event or performance. It is in the style of Thomas Rowlandson. The image shows a bustling interior with richly dressed figures engaged in various preparatory tasks. In the center, an individual is being fitted with a large gown, holding a bouquet of flowers, while others help adjust the attire. A mirror is prominently displayed, reflecting the scene, and there are accessories scattered around the floor. The expressions on the figures suggest a moment of satire or comedic intent, capturing a lively and chaotic atmosphere typical of Rowlandson's works.

artworks.title: A Frenchman in November
artworks.description: This is a drawing of three comical characters in animated poses. The scene depicts an interaction among three figures: one seated in an ornate chair wearing a green coat; a central character dressed in a blue and red coat with a large black hat, holding a horn and a whip; and the third figure on the right, dressed in brown, caught in a pose with arms raised and one leg lifted. Their expressions and movements suggest a humorous or chaotic scene. The line work is detailed, and the use of color adds to the animated feel of the composition. The style is reminiscent of 18th-century caricature art.

artworks.title: A Money Scrivener
artworks.description: The image shows a man standing next to a table, leaning forward with one hand on an open book and the other hand on his chin. He wears a red cap with a feather, a blue coat with gold trim, a white shirt, pink knee breeches, and dark shoes. Beside him, a person in gray clothing and a white cap sits at the table working. On the floor are papers, and on the desk is a pot of quills. The background includes a leaded glass window, simple walls, and writing above.

artworks.title: A Penny Barber
artworks.description: This print features a scene in a barber shop. In the center, a tall person with a pointed nose and chin wearing a large white wig holds a shaving bowl. To the right, a person covered in a white cloth sits in a chair looking upwards, their chin covered in a white substance. A person on the left in front of a large blue window appears to wash their hands in a bowl, while another in the background uses a tool to press down on a wig that rests on a mannequin head. The characters all have light skin and wear garments in blue or white. Hanging from the ceiling is a blue sign that reads "The oldest shaving shop in London, most mony for second hand wigs." There is a bird cage perched above the window on the left.

artworks.title: A Cart Race
artworks.description: This is a painting of a chaotic cart race on a village street. Three horse-drawn carts are in a race with horses galloping energetically, wheels turning wildly, and debris flying in the air. Competitors are in dynamic poses with expressions of excitement or distress. Some passengers are tumbling out of the carts. The background shows quaint houses with onlookers, some leaning out of windows. The sky is clear blue with a few clouds, adding to the lively atmosphere. This is in the style of Thomas Rowlandson.

artworks.title: The High-mettled Racer
artworks.description: This is a painting of a horse race scene featuring riders speeding across the scene, surrounded by a crowd of spectators. In the foreground, a rider in a yellow jacket is prominently featured on a white horse, with several other riders on brown horses racing beside him. The spectators, including some on foot and others in carriages, are energetically engaged. There is movement and liveliness, enhanced by the dynamic poses of the horses and the expressions of the crowd. The background features soft sky blues and muted earth tones, adding depth and contrast. This painting is in the style of James Gillray.

artworks.title: The Course
artworks.description: The image shows a group of elegantly dressed individuals on horses. There are cumulus clouds in the sky and more horses and riders in the distance. The brushwork shows fine detailing of the clothing and horses, with a gentle color palette of soft blues and creams in the sky, and earthy tones in the attire and horses.

artworks.title: The Overdrove Ox
artworks.description: This is a painting of a chaotic street scene involving an overdriven ox. The scene depicts an ox causing havoc amongst a crowd and several horses, with a backdrop that includes a church tower and a vista of ships in a harbor. People are shown in various states of distress and activity as the ox runs amok. The composition is dynamic with numerous details portraying the bustling confusion of the event, including a cart labelled "Crockford London Atheneum AMA".

artworks.title: The Enamoured Sportsman
artworks.description: The image shows two people, a man and a woman, with both their upper bodies in view and extending to their knees. The woman is seated at the base of a tree, facing slightly to her left, dressed in a pale blue gown with long sleeves and an ornate white lace collar. Her hair is blonde, long, and curly, with a bonnet tied with a pink ribbon. The man is kneeling beside her right side, wearing a coral pink coat with brass buttons and a white cravat, and his hair is light-colored with gentle curls. He looks up towards the woman, holding her hands. Gold bands are visible on each of her wrists. Behind them stands a horse with a brown coat, along with the wheel of a carriage and a tree trunk. The scene is framed by lush green foliage with a landscape visible in the distance under a blue sky.

artworks.title: First and Second Floor
artworks.description: The image shows illustrations of four women positioned at two different windows. Two women lean out of a window with an open pane, one resting both arms on the window sill wearing a wide-brimmed hat with large pink flowers, and the other with curly hair, wearing a cap and leaning with one arm on the sill and the other hand on her hip. The other two women are seen at another window, dressed in elaborate 18th-century clothing with lace and ruffles. One wears a green feathered headpiece and the other wears a blue feathered piece in her hair. A stone or brick wall serves as the backdrop, with the lower window having a sash frame and being partially draped with curtains. Text beneath the image labels it as "First & Second Floor".

artworks.title: The Prospect before us, No. 2
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a theatrical performance in a grand theater. The drawing features a scene set in an elaborate theater with a highly detailed audience filling the multi-tiered balconies. Two central figures are depicted on stage, energetically dancing and holding garlands of flowers. The theater is grand, with intricately designed boxes and a chandelier on the sides. The audience is animated, each person expressing different emotions as they watch the performance. The overall tone of the drawing is vibrant and lively.

artworks.title: A Little Tighter
artworks.description: The image depicts two people in a dynamic pose. One person is wearing a white dress with a pink bodice and has curly hair with a large feather. The other person is in motion, wearing a blue coat and yellow stockings. Both have round faces with distinct facial features. The smaller person is leaning backward, reaching upward. A tricorn hat lies on the floor. The background is plain and light gray to highlight the figures.

artworks.title: Slugs in a Sawpit
artworks.description: This is a painting of two men facing each other in a saw-pit, engaged in a confrontation through a telescope-like device. The figure on the left wears a blue coat with gold trimming and a tricorne hat, while the figure on the right is in a red coat with a black hat. They appear to be scrutinizing each other through the shared object. The setting is a saw-pit with wood shavings, saws, and a ladder leading out. The expressions and postures of the figures convey a sense of absurdity and satire. In the background, a third figure peers over the edge of the pit. The painting features expressive lines and subtle coloring, typical of satirical work from the late 18th century. This follows the style of Thomas Rowlandson.

artworks.title: Mr. H. Angelo's Fencing Academy
artworks.description: This is a painting of a scene in a fencing academy. The image shows a lively interior of a fencing school where several figures are engaged in and observing a swordfight. The room is filled with fencing-related items, such as masks and foils, and portraits decorating the walls. The composition captures the energy and movement of the duelists while emphasizing the elaborate attire of the spectators. This is in the style of Thomas Rowlandson, known for his humorous and satirical depictions of social scenes.

artworks.title: A Squall in Hyde Park
artworks.description: This is a painting of a street scene with a carriage and pedestrians in a bustling setting. The scene conveys a sense of chaos with people and animals reacting to something happening in the street. Some people appear disarrayed, with hats and umbrellas flying in the air. The background shows residential buildings with blue roofs and trees. The style resembles that of Thomas Rowlandson, known for caricatures and social commentary through humorous depictions.
